account: It is day 1, nine in the morning, and I am holding office at town hall before the ten o'clock mill grain inspection. The baker has come to offer bread for meetings or meals, at one emerald per loaf, and says the bread was baked yesterday. I have said no order is needed. The neighbour also visited, but I could not make out their words and they are now farther away. I should not assume their purpose. The builder earlier asked about paid repair work but reported no confirmed defects, including none reported by the baker or innkeeper. No work or transport has been authorized. The secretary has filed search findings after receiving stationery money and is keeping the appointments in order. What remains unusual to me is the absence of the accounts ledger and any verified record of outstanding commitments: the four great-hall chests were empty, and neither the secretary nor builder knows where the ledger is or who previously kept it. This could be poor recordkeeping; it is not evidence of a secret gathering or wrongdoing. I still feel I may be missing town news, but no one has supplied a specific occasion, date, or confirmed unusual activity. The visits so far are consistent with ordinary trade and office business. I need to hear the neighbour's actual business, read the filed findings, and keep today's appointments rather than turn suspicions into facts.
